title: Light Schrödinger Bridge

en.text: A Schrödinger Bridge asks a deceptively simple question: given two probability distributions, what is the most natural stochastic path that carries one into the other? "Most natural" here means the diffusion process that stays as close as possible to a reference Wiener process — plain Brownian motion. This object is the dynamic form of Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT), and it turns up all over applied machine learning, from tracking how single cells differentiate over time, to unpaired image translation, to generative modeling.

The catch is that actually computing a Schrödinger Bridge has become an exercise in heavy machinery. Most modern solvers stack several neural networks, lean on adversarial min-max objectives or iterative proportional fitting (IPF), and simulate the full stochastic process at every training step. They demand careful network design, run for hours on a GPU, and are sensitive to a long list of hyperparameters. The field has powerful solvers, but it lacks a simple, principled default — the Schrödinger Bridge equivalent of k-means for clustering or Sinkhorn for discrete optimal transport, the method you reach for first before anything fancier.

The paper Light Schrödinger Bridge (LightSB), from researchers at Skoltech and AIRI, sets out to be exactly that baseline. Its move is to parameterize the Schrödinger potential as a Gaussian mixture and treat the logarithm of that potential as an energy function. Under this choice the whole problem collapses into a single, non-minimax optimization objective whose key pieces — the transport plan and the drift of the process — have closed-form expressions. The result solves Schrödinger Bridges in moderate dimensions in minutes on a CPU, needs almost no hyperparameter tuning, and is provably a universal approximator of Schrödinger Bridges.

en.caption: Figure 1. Unpaired male-to-female face translation by LightSB in the 512-dimensional ALAE latent space of 1024x1024 FFHQ images. Each row starts from one real male photo (left); because the bridge is stochastic, a single input maps to a spread of plausible outputs. Converges in under one minute on 4 CPU cores.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01174
Code: https://github.com/ngushchin/LightSB
The problem: heavy solvers, no baseline

Formally, the Schrödinger Bridge between a source distribution p0 and a target p1 is the diffusion process, pinned to those two marginals, that minimizes its Kullback-Leibler divergence from a Wiener prior. A noise level ε controls how much the process is allowed to wander: small ε keeps trajectories nearly straight and deterministic, large ε lets them diffuse widely. Solving the bridge yields both a transport plan π*(x1 | x0) — where a given starting point is likely to end up — and the full time-dependent process connecting the two ends.

In most real applications, though, only the endpoints matter. A biologist mapping cells from an early day to a later one cares about the conditional plan π*(x1 | x0) — where a cell is likely to end up — not the exact shape of every intermediate trajectory. That mismatch, heavy neural machinery for a comparatively modest goal, is the gap LightSB is built to close. It helps to picture the target in two dimensions first.

en.caption: Figure 2. A two-dimensional toy problem: LightSB is asked to bridge an input Gaussian blob (green, the source distribution p0) to a Swiss-roll ring (orange, the target distribution p1). Because the solver is lightweight, it is cheap to visualize how the noise level ε reshapes the learned process on a task like this — from near-straight transport at small ε to visibly volatile trajectories as ε grows.

en.text: How LightSB works

LightSB starts from the natural goal: directly minimize KL(π* || π_θ), the divergence between the true EOT plan and a parameterized plan π_θ. The obstacle is obvious — we do not know the true plan π*. The key observation is that we do not have to. The optimal plan is known to factor as π_θ(x1 | x0) proportional to exp(<x0, x1> / ε) · v_θ(x1), so all that is left to learn is the adjusted Schrödinger potential v_θ.

LightSB parameterizes that potential as an unnormalized Gaussian mixture, v_θ(x1) = Σ_k α_k · N(x1 | r_k, ε S_k). This single choice makes two otherwise-intractable quantities available in closed form: the conditional distributions of the plan, π_θ(x1 | x0), and the normalization constant c_θ(x0). With those in hand, the KL objective rewrites as a simple difference of two expectations — the log-normalization averaged over the source and the log-potential averaged over the target — which can be estimated by Monte Carlo from samples and then minimized with ordinary stochastic gradient descent (SGD), the same workhorse optimizer used to train any standard neural network.
L(θ) = E_{x0 ~ p0}[ log c_θ(x0) ] − E_{x1 ~ p1}[ log v_θ(x1) ]

There is no min-max game, no iterative proportional fitting, and no simulation of trajectories during training — the three ingredients that make earlier solvers slow and fragile. And because the same learned potential yields a closed-form drift, the full bridge process can be reconstructed after the fact whenever the intermediate dynamics are actually needed. The authors also prove that this Gaussian-mixture solver is a universal approximator of Schrödinger Bridges — they note it is the first such result — and show its generalization error vanishes at the standard parametric rate as the sample size grows.
Results: accuracy and speed

The first test is a benchmark where the ground-truth plan is actually known (Gushchin et al., 2023b), spanning dimensions D = 2 to 128 and noise levels ε = 0.1, 1, 10. Here LightSB is not merely competitive — it wins by a wide margin. Its conditional Bures-Wasserstein error (cBW-squared-UVP) lands between roughly 0.03% and 0.62%, while the best prior solver ranges from about 1.04% up to 18.05%. When the target aligns with LightSB's Gaussian-mixture inductive bias, the gap is largest.

The more striking result is speed. On the MSCI single-cell dataset — cells from four human donors across several days, projected by PCA to 50, 100, and 1000 dimensions — LightSB matches strong GPU-based solvers in energy distance while training on just 4 CPU cores in 65 to 146 seconds, versus roughly 8 to 71 minutes on a V100 GPU for the continuous baselines. The hardest setting makes the contrast concrete: an energy distance of 1.27 on CPU against 1.32 for a minimax GPU solver, at a fraction of the wall-clock cost.

en.caption: Table 1. MSCI single-cell task at DIM = 1000: LightSB matches a strong minimax GPU solver on energy distance while training on CPU in a fraction of the wall-clock time (numbers from the paper).

en.text: The same lightness carries over to a much higher-dimensional problem: unpaired face translation in the 512-dimensional latent space of a pretrained ALAE autoencoder. LightSB performs male-to-female and adult-to-child translation there, again converging in under a minute on 4 CPU cores. Because the plan is stochastic, a single input face yields a spread of plausible outputs rather than one fixed answer, which is exactly what a well-behaved stochastic transport plan should do.

en.caption: Figure 3. Male-to-female translation across two different source faces (left of each pair) and the samples LightSB produces (right). The translations change the target attribute while preserving identity-adjacent details — pose, lighting, expression — all learned in the ALAE latent space without paired training data.

en.text: What ε buys you

The noise level ε is the one knob that genuinely changes the character of the solution, and the 2D Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll study makes its role visible. Sweeping ε across small to larger values (the paper uses 2·10⁻³, 10⁻², 10⁻¹), small ε produces nearly straight, almost deterministic trajectories that map each source point to a tight endpoint; as ε grows, trajectories become more volatile and the conditional distributions π_θ(x1 | x0) spread out. This is exactly the behavior the theory predicts — ε is the dial for how stochastic the bridge is — and it means a user can pick ε to match how much diversity they want in the output, rather than tuning it just to appease a finicky optimizer.
The takeaway

The lasting message of LightSB is that a Schrödinger Bridge solver does not have to be heavy. By writing the transport potential as a Gaussian mixture and minimizing one straightforward objective, LightSB solves entropic optimal transport and Schrödinger Bridges in minutes on a CPU — no adversarial training, no process simulation, and little tuning — while matching or beating much heavier GPU-based solvers and carrying a universal-approximation guarantee.

The honest boundary is scope. LightSB targets moderate-dimensional distributions, and its image results live in a pretrained autoencoder's latent space rather than in raw pixel space, so it is a transport solver rather than a from-scratch image generator. Within that scope, though, it does something the field had been missing: it offers a simple, fast, reliable default — the baseline you can run first, on the hardware you already have, before deciding whether a heavier solver is worth it.

zh.text: Schrödinger Bridge（薛定谔桥）想回答一个看似简单的问题：给定两个概率分布，把其中一个「搬」到另一个上，最自然的随机路径是什么？这里的「最自然」，指的是在所有满足两端边缘分布的扩散过程中，与参考的 Wiener 过程（也就是普通布朗运动）最接近的那一个。它是熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport，EOT）的动态形式，在机器学习里出现得非常频繁：从追踪单细胞随时间的分化，到无配对的图像风格迁移，再到生成模型。

问题在于，真正把一个 Schrödinger Bridge 算出来，如今几乎成了「重装备」的代名词。主流求解器往往要堆叠好几个神经网络，依赖对抗式的 min-max 目标或迭代比例拟合（IPF），并且在训练的每一步都要模拟整条随机过程。它们需要精心设计网络结构，在 GPU 上一跑就是几个小时，还对一长串超参数很敏感。这个领域有很强的求解器，却始终缺一个简单、可靠的默认基线，也就是 Schrödinger Bridge 版本的「k-means / Sinkhorn」，那种你会最先拿来一试、之后再考虑要不要上更复杂方法的工具。

来自 Skoltech 与 AIRI 的论文 Light Schrödinger Bridge（LightSB），目标正是成为这样一个基线。它的核心思路是：把 Schrödinger 势函数（Schrödinger potential）参数化成一个高斯混合（Gaussian mixture），再把这个势函数的对数看作一个能量函数（energy function）。在这样的选择下，整个问题坍缩成一个非 min-max 的单一优化目标，而其中最关键的两部分：传输计划与过程的漂移项（drift），都能写出闭式表达式。最终，它在中等维度上几分钟内、仅用 CPU 就能求解 Schrödinger Bridge，几乎不用调参，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器（universal approximator）。

zh.caption: 图1 LightSB 在 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中完成的无配对「男→女」人脸迁移（1024x1024 的 FFHQ 图像）。每行最左为真实男性照片；由于桥是随机的，同一个输入会对应一片合理输出。4 个 CPU 核心上不到 1 分钟收敛。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01174
代码：https://github.com/ngushchin/LightSB
问题：求解器很重，却没有基线

严格来说，源分布 p0 与目标分布 p1 之间的 Schrödinger Bridge，就是在被这两个边缘分布「钉住」的所有扩散过程里，与 Wiener 先验的 KL 散度最小的那一个。噪声水平 ε 决定了过程可以「乱走」到什么程度：ε 小，轨迹几乎笔直、近似确定性；ε 大，轨迹就会明显扩散。解出这座桥，同时会得到一个传输计划 π*(x1 | x0)（某个起点最可能落到哪里），以及连接两端的完整时间演化过程。
但在多数实际应用里，人们真正在意的只有两端。做单细胞研究的人想把早期某天的细胞映射到较晚某天，做图像迁移的人想把一个域翻译成另一个域，他们关心的是条件计划 π*(x1 | x0)，而不是每条中间轨迹的精确形状。「用很重的神经网络去完成一个其实并不复杂的目标」，这种错配正是 LightSB 想要弥合的落差。要建立直觉，不妨先在二维上看看它要连接的是什么。

zh.caption: 图2 一个二维玩具问题：让 LightSB 把输入的高斯分布（绿色，源分布 p0）搭桥到瑞士卷形状的目标（橙色，目标分布 p1）。正因为求解器足够轻，才能低成本地在这种任务上观察噪声水平 ε 如何改变学到的过程：ε 小时传输近乎笔直，ε 增大时轨迹会明显变得更「摇摆」。

zh.text: LightSB 是怎么做到的

LightSB 从最自然的目标出发：直接最小化 KL(π* || π_θ)，也就是真实 EOT 计划 π* 与参数化计划 π_θ 之间的散度。障碍很明显：我们并不知道真实计划 π*。关键的观察是，其实不需要知道。最优计划有已知的形式，可以写成 π_θ(x1 | x0) 正比于 exp(<x0, x1> / ε) · v_θ(x1)，于是唯一还需要学习的对象，就只剩下那个调整之后的 Schrödinger 势函数 v_θ。换句话说，这一步把问题从「学习整个传输计划」缩小成了「只学习一个势函数」。

LightSB 把这个势函数参数化成一个未归一化的高斯混合：v_θ(x1) = Σ_k α_k · N(x1 | r_k, ε S_k)。仅这一个选择，就让两个原本难算的量变得有闭式解：计划的条件分布 π_θ(x1 | x0)，以及归一化常数 c_θ(x0)。有了它们，KL 目标就能改写成两个期望之差，即在源分布上取 log 归一化常数、在目标分布上取 log 势函数，两者都能用样本做 Monte Carlo 估计，并用普通的随机梯度下降（SGD）来最小化。
L(θ) = E_{x0 ~ p0}[ log c_θ(x0) ] − E_{x1 ~ p1}[ log v_θ(x1) ]
整个过程没有 min-max 博弈，没有迭代比例拟合，训练时也不需要模拟任何轨迹，而这三样恰恰是过去求解器又慢又脆的根源。又因为同一个学到的势函数能直接给出闭式的漂移项，一旦真的需要中间动态，完整的桥过程可以在事后重建出来。作者还证明了这个高斯混合求解器是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器（并指出这是首个此类结果），并说明其泛化误差会以标准的参数收敛速率随样本量增加而消失。
结果：既准又快

第一项测试用的是一个已知真实计划的基准（Gushchin et al., 2023b），覆盖维度 D = 2 到 128、噪声水平 ε = 0.1、1、10。在这里 LightSB 不只是有竞争力，而是大幅领先：它的条件 Bures-Wasserstein 误差（cBW-squared-UVP）落在约 0.03% 到 0.62% 之间，而此前最好的求解器则在约 1.04% 到 18.05% 之间。当目标分布越贴合 LightSB 的高斯混合归纳偏置，这个差距就越大。

更抢眼的是速度。在 MSCI 单细胞数据集上（来自四位捐赠者、跨越多天的细胞，经 PCA 投影到 50、100、1000 维），LightSB 在能量距离（energy distance）上与强大的 GPU 求解器持平，却只用 4 个 CPU 核心、耗时 65 到 146 秒完成训练，而那些连续型基线在 V100 GPU 上大约需要 8 到 71 分钟。最难的设置最能说明问题：CPU 上的能量距离为 1.27，而一个 min-max GPU 求解器为 1.32，两者相当，但 LightSB 的训练耗时只是后者的零头。

zh.caption: 表1（DIM = 1000 的 MSCI 单细胞任务）：LightSB 在能量距离上追平一个强大的 min-max GPU 求解器，训练却只用 CPU、耗时只是其零头（数据取自论文）。

zh.text: 同样的「轻」也延续到了维度高得多的问题上：在预训练 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中做无配对人脸迁移。LightSB 在这里完成「男→女」与「成人→儿童」的迁移，同样在 4 个 CPU 核心上不到一分钟就收敛。由于计划是随机的，一张输入人脸会得到一片合理的输出，而不是唯一确定的结果。

zh.caption: 图3 两张不同源人脸（每对的左侧）上的「男→女」迁移，以及 LightSB 给出的结果（右侧）。迁移在改变目标属性的同时，保留了姿态、光照、表情等与身份相邻的细节，全部在 ALAE 隐空间中、无需配对训练数据学得。

zh.text: ε 到底带来了什么

噪声水平 ε 是真正会改变解的「性格」的那个旋钮，而二维「高斯→瑞士卷」的研究把它的作用直接可视化了出来。把 ε 从小到大扫过一遍（论文取 2·10⁻³、10⁻²、10⁻¹）：ε 小时，轨迹几乎笔直、近乎确定性，把每个源点映射到一个很集中的终点；ε 增大，轨迹变得更摇摆，条件分布 π_θ(x1 | x0) 也随之铺开。这正是理论预期的行为，ε 就是控制桥有多随机的那个刻度。这也意味着，用户可以根据自己想要多大的输出多样性来选 ε，而不是为了迁就优化器去调它。
小结
LightSB 留下的核心讯息是：Schrödinger Bridge 求解器并不一定要「重」。把传输势函数写成高斯混合、再最小化一个直白的目标，LightSB 就能在 CPU 上几分钟内求解熵正则最优传输与 Schrödinger Bridge，无需对抗训练、无需过程模拟、几乎不用调参，同时追平甚至超过重得多的 GPU 求解器，还带着通用逼近的理论保证。
需要诚实说明的是它的边界，也就是适用范围。LightSB 面向的是中等维度的分布，其图像结果生活在预训练自编码器的隐空间里，而非原始像素空间，所以它是一个传输求解器，而不是一个从零开始的图像生成器。但在这个范围之内，它做到了这个领域一直缺的一件事：提供一个简单、快速、可靠的默认基线，一个你可以先在手头现有硬件上跑一遍，再决定是否值得上更重方案的起点。

严格来说，源分布 p0 与目标分布 p1 之间的 Schrödinger Bridge，就是在被这两个边缘分布「钉住」的所有扩散过程里，与 Wiener 先验的 KL 散度最小的那一个。噪声水平 ε 决定了过程可以「乱走」到什么程度：ε 小，轨迹几乎笔直、近似确定性；ε 大，轨迹就会明显扩散。解出这座桥，同时会得到一个传输计划 π*(x1 | x0)（某个起点最可能落到哪里），以及连接两端的完整时间演化过程。
但在多数实际应用里，人们真正在意的只有两端。做单细胞研究的人想把早期某天的细胞映射到较晚某天，做图像迁移的人想把一个域翻译成另一个域，他们关心的是条件计划 π*(x1 | x0)，而不是每条中间轨迹的精确形状。「用很重的神经网络去完成一个其实并不复杂的目标」，这种错配正是 LightSB 想要弥合的落差。要建立直觉，不妨先在二维上看看它要连接的是什么。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 一台笔记本就能解的 Schrödinger Bridge
zh.subtitle: LightSB 把熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport）压缩成一个高斯混合目标：CPU 上几分钟出结果，无需对抗训练，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器。

en.caption: Figure 1. Unpaired male-to-female face translation by LightSB in the 512-dimensional ALAE latent space of 1024x1024 FFHQ images. Each row starts from one real male photo (left); because the bridge is stochastic, a single input maps to a spread of plausible outputs. Converges in under one minute on 4 CPU cores.

en.text: How LightSB works

LightSB starts from the natural goal: directly minimize KL(π* || π_θ), the divergence between the true EOT plan and a parameterized plan π_θ. The obstacle is obvious — we do not know the true plan π*. The key observation is that we do not have to. The optimal plan is known to factor as π_θ(x1 | x0) proportional to exp(<x0, x1> / ε) · v_θ(x1), so all that is left to learn is the adjusted Schrödinger potential v_θ.

LightSB parameterizes that potential as an unnormalized Gaussian mixture, v_θ(x1) = Σ_k α_k · N(x1 | r_k, ε S_k). This single choice makes two otherwise-intractable quantities available in closed form: the conditional distributions of the plan, π_θ(x1 | x0), and the normalization constant c_θ(x0). With those in hand, the KL objective rewrites as a simple difference of two expectations — the log-normalization averaged over the source and the log-potential averaged over the target — which can be estimated by Monte Carlo from samples and then minimized with ordinary stochastic gradient descent (SGD), the same workhorse optimizer used to train any standard neural network.
L(θ) = E_{x0 ~ p0}[ log c_θ(x0) ] − E_{x1 ~ p1}[ log v_θ(x1) ]

There is no min-max game, no iterative proportional fitting, and no simulation of trajectories during training — the three ingredients that make earlier solvers slow and fragile. And because the same learned potential yields a closed-form drift, the full bridge process can be reconstructed after the fact whenever the intermediate dynamics are actually needed. The authors also prove that this Gaussian-mixture solver is a universal approximator of Schrödinger Bridges — they note it is the first such result — and show its generalization error vanishes at the standard parametric rate as the sample size grows.

zh.caption: 图1 LightSB 在 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中完成的无配对「男→女」人脸迁移（1024x1024 的 FFHQ 图像）。每行最左为真实男性照片；由于桥是随机的，同一个输入会对应一片合理输出。4 个 CPU 核心上不到 1 分钟收敛。

zh.text: LightSB 是怎么做到的

LightSB 从最自然的目标出发：直接最小化 KL(π* || π_θ)，也就是真实 EOT 计划 π* 与参数化计划 π_θ 之间的散度。障碍很明显：我们并不知道真实计划 π*。关键的观察是，其实不需要知道。最优计划有已知的形式，可以写成 π_θ(x1 | x0) 正比于 exp(<x0, x1> / ε) · v_θ(x1)，于是唯一还需要学习的对象，就只剩下那个调整之后的 Schrödinger 势函数 v_θ。换句话说，这一步把问题从「学习整个传输计划」缩小成了「只学习一个势函数」。

LightSB 把这个势函数参数化成一个未归一化的高斯混合：v_θ(x1) = Σ_k α_k · N(x1 | r_k, ε S_k)。仅这一个选择，就让两个原本难算的量变得有闭式解：计划的条件分布 π_θ(x1 | x0)，以及归一化常数 c_θ(x0)。有了它们，KL 目标就能改写成两个期望之差，即在源分布上取 log 归一化常数、在目标分布上取 log 势函数，两者都能用样本做 Monte Carlo 估计，并用普通的随机梯度下降（SGD）来最小化。
L(θ) = E_{x0 ~ p0}[ log c_θ(x0) ] − E_{x1 ~ p1}[ log v_θ(x1) ]
整个过程没有 min-max 博弈，没有迭代比例拟合，训练时也不需要模拟任何轨迹，而这三样恰恰是过去求解器又慢又脆的根源。又因为同一个学到的势函数能直接给出闭式的漂移项，一旦真的需要中间动态，完整的桥过程可以在事后重建出来。作者还证明了这个高斯混合求解器是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器（并指出这是首个此类结果），并说明其泛化误差会以标准的参数收敛速率随样本量增加而消失。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 一台笔记本就能解的 Schrödinger Bridge
zh.subtitle: LightSB 把熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport）压缩成一个高斯混合目标：CPU 上几分钟出结果，无需对抗训练，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器。

en.text: A Schrödinger Bridge asks a deceptively simple question: given two probability distributions, what is the most natural stochastic path that carries one into the other? "Most natural" here means the diffusion process that stays as close as possible to a reference Wiener process — plain Brownian motion. This object is the dynamic form of Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT), and it turns up all over applied machine learning, from tracking how single cells differentiate over time, to unpaired image translation, to generative modeling.

The catch is that actually computing a Schrödinger Bridge has become an exercise in heavy machinery. Most modern solvers stack several neural networks, lean on adversarial min-max objectives or iterative proportional fitting (IPF), and simulate the full stochastic process at every training step. They demand careful network design, run for hours on a GPU, and are sensitive to a long list of hyperparameters. The field has powerful solvers, but it lacks a simple, principled default — the Schrödinger Bridge equivalent of k-means for clustering or Sinkhorn for discrete optimal transport, the method you reach for first before anything fancier.

The paper Light Schrödinger Bridge (LightSB), from researchers at Skoltech and AIRI, sets out to be exactly that baseline. Its move is to parameterize the Schrödinger potential as a Gaussian mixture and treat the logarithm of that potential as an energy function. Under this choice the whole problem collapses into a single, non-minimax optimization objective whose key pieces — the transport plan and the drift of the process — have closed-form expressions. The result solves Schrödinger Bridges in moderate dimensions in minutes on a CPU, needs almost no hyperparameter tuning, and is provably a universal approximator of Schrödinger Bridges.

en.caption: Figure 1. Unpaired male-to-female face translation by LightSB in the 512-dimensional ALAE latent space of 1024x1024 FFHQ images. Each row starts from one real male photo (left); because the bridge is stochastic, a single input maps to a spread of plausible outputs. Converges in under one minute on 4 CPU cores.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01174
Code: https://github.com/ngushchin/LightSB
The takeaway

The lasting message of LightSB is that a Schrödinger Bridge solver does not have to be heavy. By writing the transport potential as a Gaussian mixture and minimizing one straightforward objective, LightSB solves entropic optimal transport and Schrödinger Bridges in minutes on a CPU — no adversarial training, no process simulation, and little tuning — while matching or beating much heavier GPU-based solvers and carrying a universal-approximation guarantee.

The honest boundary is scope. LightSB targets moderate-dimensional distributions, and its image results live in a pretrained autoencoder's latent space rather than in raw pixel space, so it is a transport solver rather than a from-scratch image generator. Within that scope, though, it does something the field had been missing: it offers a simple, fast, reliable default — the baseline you can run first, on the hardware you already have, before deciding whether a heavier solver is worth it.

zh.text: Schrödinger Bridge（薛定谔桥）想回答一个看似简单的问题：给定两个概率分布，把其中一个「搬」到另一个上，最自然的随机路径是什么？这里的「最自然」，指的是在所有满足两端边缘分布的扩散过程中，与参考的 Wiener 过程（也就是普通布朗运动）最接近的那一个。它是熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport，EOT）的动态形式，在机器学习里出现得非常频繁：从追踪单细胞随时间的分化，到无配对的图像风格迁移，再到生成模型。

问题在于，真正把一个 Schrödinger Bridge 算出来，如今几乎成了「重装备」的代名词。主流求解器往往要堆叠好几个神经网络，依赖对抗式的 min-max 目标或迭代比例拟合（IPF），并且在训练的每一步都要模拟整条随机过程。它们需要精心设计网络结构，在 GPU 上一跑就是几个小时，还对一长串超参数很敏感。这个领域有很强的求解器，却始终缺一个简单、可靠的默认基线，也就是 Schrödinger Bridge 版本的「k-means / Sinkhorn」，那种你会最先拿来一试、之后再考虑要不要上更复杂方法的工具。

来自 Skoltech 与 AIRI 的论文 Light Schrödinger Bridge（LightSB），目标正是成为这样一个基线。它的核心思路是：把 Schrödinger 势函数（Schrödinger potential）参数化成一个高斯混合（Gaussian mixture），再把这个势函数的对数看作一个能量函数（energy function）。在这样的选择下，整个问题坍缩成一个非 min-max 的单一优化目标，而其中最关键的两部分：传输计划与过程的漂移项（drift），都能写出闭式表达式。最终，它在中等维度上几分钟内、仅用 CPU 就能求解 Schrödinger Bridge，几乎不用调参，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器（universal approximator）。

zh.caption: 图1 LightSB 在 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中完成的无配对「男→女」人脸迁移（1024x1024 的 FFHQ 图像）。每行最左为真实男性照片；由于桥是随机的，同一个输入会对应一片合理输出。4 个 CPU 核心上不到 1 分钟收敛。

代码：https://github.com/ngushchin/LightSB

en.subtitle: LightSB collapses entropic optimal transport into a single Gaussian-mixture objective — minutes on a CPU, no adversarial training, with a universal-approximation guarantee.

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 一台笔记本就能解的 Schrödinger Bridge
zh.subtitle: LightSB 把熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport）压缩成一个高斯混合目标：CPU 上几分钟出结果，无需对抗训练，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器。

en.text: Results: accuracy and speed

The first test is a benchmark where the ground-truth plan is actually known (Gushchin et al., 2023b), spanning dimensions D = 2 to 128 and noise levels ε = 0.1, 1, 10. Here LightSB is not merely competitive — it wins by a wide margin. Its conditional Bures-Wasserstein error (cBW-squared-UVP) lands between roughly 0.03% and 0.62%, while the best prior solver ranges from about 1.04% up to 18.05%. When the target aligns with LightSB's Gaussian-mixture inductive bias, the gap is largest.

The more striking result is speed. On the MSCI single-cell dataset — cells from four human donors across several days, projected by PCA to 50, 100, and 1000 dimensions — LightSB matches strong GPU-based solvers in energy distance while training on just 4 CPU cores in 65 to 146 seconds, versus roughly 8 to 71 minutes on a V100 GPU for the continuous baselines. The hardest setting makes the contrast concrete: an energy distance of 1.27 on CPU against 1.32 for a minimax GPU solver, at a fraction of the wall-clock cost.

en.caption: Table 1. MSCI single-cell task at DIM = 1000: LightSB matches a strong minimax GPU solver on energy distance while training on CPU in a fraction of the wall-clock time (numbers from the paper).

en.text: The same lightness carries over to a much higher-dimensional problem: unpaired face translation in the 512-dimensional latent space of a pretrained ALAE autoencoder. LightSB performs male-to-female and adult-to-child translation there, again converging in under a minute on 4 CPU cores. Because the plan is stochastic, a single input face yields a spread of plausible outputs rather than one fixed answer, which is exactly what a well-behaved stochastic transport plan should do.

en.caption: Figure 3. Male-to-female translation across two different source faces (left of each pair) and the samples LightSB produces (right). The translations change the target attribute while preserving identity-adjacent details — pose, lighting, expression — all learned in the ALAE latent space without paired training data.

zh.text: 结果：既准又快

第一项测试用的是一个已知真实计划的基准（Gushchin et al., 2023b），覆盖维度 D = 2 到 128、噪声水平 ε = 0.1、1、10。在这里 LightSB 不只是有竞争力，而是大幅领先：它的条件 Bures-Wasserstein 误差（cBW-squared-UVP）落在约 0.03% 到 0.62% 之间，而此前最好的求解器则在约 1.04% 到 18.05% 之间。当目标分布越贴合 LightSB 的高斯混合归纳偏置，这个差距就越大。

更抢眼的是速度。在 MSCI 单细胞数据集上（来自四位捐赠者、跨越多天的细胞，经 PCA 投影到 50、100、1000 维），LightSB 在能量距离（energy distance）上与强大的 GPU 求解器持平，却只用 4 个 CPU 核心、耗时 65 到 146 秒完成训练，而那些连续型基线在 V100 GPU 上大约需要 8 到 71 分钟。最难的设置最能说明问题：CPU 上的能量距离为 1.27，而一个 min-max GPU 求解器为 1.32，两者相当，但 LightSB 的训练耗时只是后者的零头。

zh.caption: 表1（DIM = 1000 的 MSCI 单细胞任务）：LightSB 在能量距离上追平一个强大的 min-max GPU 求解器，训练却只用 CPU、耗时只是其零头（数据取自论文）。

zh.text: 同样的「轻」也延续到了维度高得多的问题上：在预训练 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中做无配对人脸迁移。LightSB 在这里完成「男→女」与「成人→儿童」的迁移，同样在 4 个 CPU 核心上不到一分钟就收敛。由于计划是随机的，一张输入人脸会得到一片合理的输出，而不是唯一确定的结果。

zh.caption: 图3 两张不同源人脸（每对的左侧）上的「男→女」迁移，以及 LightSB 给出的结果（右侧）。迁移在改变目标属性的同时，保留了姿态、光照、表情等与身份相邻的细节，全部在 ALAE 隐空间中、无需配对训练数据学得。

zh.text: 同样的「轻」也延续到了维度高得多的问题上：在预训练 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中做无配对人脸迁移。LightSB 在这里完成「男→女」与「成人→儿童」的迁移，同样在 4 个 CPU 核心上不到一分钟就收敛。由于计划是随机的，一张输入人脸会得到一片合理的输出，而不是唯一确定的结果。

zh.caption: 图3 两张不同源人脸（每对的左侧）上的「男→女」迁移，以及 LightSB 给出的结果（右侧）。迁移在改变目标属性的同时，保留了姿态、光照、表情等与身份相邻的细节，全部在 ALAE 隐空间中、无需配对训练数据学得。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 一台笔记本就能解的 Schrödinger Bridge
zh.subtitle: LightSB 把熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport）压缩成一个高斯混合目标：CPU 上几分钟出结果，无需对抗训练，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器。

en.text: The problem: heavy solvers, no baseline

Formally, the Schrödinger Bridge between a source distribution p0 and a target p1 is the diffusion process, pinned to those two marginals, that minimizes its Kullback-Leibler divergence from a Wiener prior. A noise level ε controls how much the process is allowed to wander: small ε keeps trajectories nearly straight and deterministic, large ε lets them diffuse widely. Solving the bridge yields both a transport plan π*(x1 | x0) — where a given starting point is likely to end up — and the full time-dependent process connecting the two ends.

In most real applications, though, only the endpoints matter. A biologist mapping cells from an early day to a later one cares about the conditional plan π*(x1 | x0) — where a cell is likely to end up — not the exact shape of every intermediate trajectory. That mismatch, heavy neural machinery for a comparatively modest goal, is the gap LightSB is built to close. It helps to picture the target in two dimensions first.

en.caption: Figure 2. A two-dimensional toy problem: LightSB is asked to bridge an input Gaussian blob (green, the source distribution p0) to a Swiss-roll ring (orange, the target distribution p1). Because the solver is lightweight, it is cheap to visualize how the noise level ε reshapes the learned process on a task like this — from near-straight transport at small ε to visibly volatile trajectories as ε grows.

zh.caption: 图1 LightSB 在 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中完成的无配对「男→女」人脸迁移（1024x1024 的 FFHQ 图像）。每行最左为真实男性照片；由于桥是随机的，同一个输入会对应一片合理输出。4 个 CPU 核心上不到 1 分钟收敛。

zh.text: LightSB 是怎么做到的

LightSB 从最自然的目标出发：直接最小化 KL(π* || π_θ)，也就是真实 EOT 计划 π* 与参数化计划 π_θ 之间的散度。障碍很明显：我们并不知道真实计划 π*。关键的观察是，其实不需要知道。最优计划有已知的形式，可以写成 π_θ(x1 | x0) 正比于 exp(<x0, x1> / ε) · v_θ(x1)，于是唯一还需要学习的对象，就只剩下那个调整之后的 Schrödinger 势函数 v_θ。换句话说，这一步把问题从「学习整个传输计划」缩小成了「只学习一个势函数」。

LightSB 把这个势函数参数化成一个未归一化的高斯混合：v_θ(x1) = Σ_k α_k · N(x1 | r_k, ε S_k)。仅这一个选择，就让两个原本难算的量变得有闭式解：计划的条件分布 π_θ(x1 | x0)，以及归一化常数 c_θ(x0)。有了它们，KL 目标就能改写成两个期望之差，即在源分布上取 log 归一化常数、在目标分布上取 log 势函数，两者都能用样本做 Monte Carlo 估计，并用普通的随机梯度下降（SGD）来最小化。
L(θ) = E_{x0 ~ p0}[ log c_θ(x0) ] − E_{x1 ~ p1}[ log v_θ(x1) ]
整个过程没有 min-max 博弈，没有迭代比例拟合，训练时也不需要模拟任何轨迹，而这三样恰恰是过去求解器又慢又脆的根源。又因为同一个学到的势函数能直接给出闭式的漂移项，一旦真的需要中间动态，完整的桥过程可以在事后重建出来。作者还证明了这个高斯混合求解器是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器（并指出这是首个此类结果），并说明其泛化误差会以标准的参数收敛速率随样本量增加而消失。

zh.subtitle: LightSB 把熵正则最优传输（Entropic Optimal Transport）压缩成一个高斯混合目标：CPU 上几分钟出结果，无需对抗训练，并且被证明是 Schrödinger Bridge 的通用逼近器。

en.caption: Figure 3. Male-to-female translation across two different source faces (left of each pair) and the samples LightSB produces (right). The translations change the target attribute while preserving identity-adjacent details — pose, lighting, expression — all learned in the ALAE latent space without paired training data.

en.text: How LightSB works

LightSB starts from the natural goal: directly minimize KL(π* || π_θ), the divergence between the true EOT plan and a parameterized plan π_θ. The obstacle is obvious — we do not know the true plan π*. The key observation is that we do not have to. The optimal plan is known to factor as π_θ(x1 | x0) proportional to exp(<x0, x1> / ε) · v_θ(x1), so all that is left to learn is the adjusted Schrödinger potential v_θ.

LightSB parameterizes that potential as an unnormalized Gaussian mixture, v_θ(x1) = Σ_k α_k · N(x1 | r_k, ε S_k). This single choice makes two otherwise-intractable quantities available in closed form: the conditional distributions of the plan, π_θ(x1 | x0), and the normalization constant c_θ(x0). With those in hand, the KL objective rewrites as a simple difference of two expectations — the log-normalization averaged over the source and the log-potential averaged over the target — which can be estimated by Monte Carlo from samples and then minimized with ordinary stochastic gradient descent (SGD), the same workhorse optimizer used to train any standard neural network.
L(θ) = E_{x0 ~ p0}[ log c_θ(x0) ] − E_{x1 ~ p1}[ log v_θ(x1) ]

There is no min-max game, no iterative proportional fitting, and no simulation of trajectories during training — the three ingredients that make earlier solvers slow and fragile. And because the same learned potential yields a closed-form drift, the full bridge process can be reconstructed after the fact whenever the intermediate dynamics are actually needed. The authors also prove that this Gaussian-mixture solver is a universal approximator of Schrödinger Bridges — they note it is the first such result — and show its generalization error vanishes at the standard parametric rate as the sample size grows.

zh.caption: 图1 LightSB 在 ALAE 自编码器的 512 维隐空间中完成的无配对「男→女」人脸迁移（1024x1024 的 FFHQ 图像）。每行最左为真实男性照片；由于桥是随机的，同一个输入会对应一片合理输出。4 个 CPU 核心上不到 1 分钟收敛。

zh.text: 小结
LightSB 留下的核心讯息是：Schrödinger Bridge 求解器并不一定要「重」。把传输势函数写成高斯混合、再最小化一个直白的目标，LightSB 就能在 CPU 上几分钟内求解熵正则最优传输与 Schrödinger Bridge，无需对抗训练、无需过程模拟、几乎不用调参，同时追平甚至超过重得多的 GPU 求解器，还带着通用逼近的理论保证。
需要诚实说明的是它的边界，也就是适用范围。LightSB 面向的是中等维度的分布，其图像结果生活在预训练自编码器的隐空间里，而非原始像素空间，所以它是一个传输求解器，而不是一个从零开始的图像生成器。但在这个范围之内，它做到了这个领域一直缺的一件事：提供一个简单、快速、可靠的默认基线，一个你可以先在手头现有硬件上跑一遍，再决定是否值得上更重方案的起点。

en.caption: Figure 1. Unpaired male-to-female face translation by LightSB in the 512-dimensional ALAE latent space of 1024x1024 FFHQ images. Each row starts from one real male photo (left); because the bridge is stochastic, a single input maps to a spread of plausible outputs. Converges in under one minute on 4 CPU cores.

en.text: The takeaway

The lasting message of LightSB is that a Schrödinger Bridge solver does not have to be heavy. By writing the transport potential as a Gaussian mixture and minimizing one straightforward objective, LightSB solves entropic optimal transport and Schrödinger Bridges in minutes on a CPU — no adversarial training, no process simulation, and little tuning — while matching or beating much heavier GPU-based solvers and carrying a universal-approximation guarantee.

The honest boundary is scope. LightSB targets moderate-dimensional distributions, and its image results live in a pretrained autoencoder's latent space rather than in raw pixel space, so it is a transport solver rather than a from-scratch image generator. Within that scope, though, it does something the field had been missing: it offers a simple, fast, reliable default — the baseline you can run first, on the hardware you already have, before deciding whether a heavier solver is worth it.
